_comment: Mutations that re-introduce the FABRICATED ORACLE in the decision
modules and in the PWA's launch modal, one at a time.
This spec has no pytest target: the code it mutates is TypeScript, and its
tests are run by vitest. The harness accepts a 'command' for exactly that
case and keeps every other guarantee it already had -- snapshot before and
SHA-256 revert verification after.
THE SKIP RULE, PRECISELY (this comment used to overclaim):
* A NEEDLE that is not found in the file is a SKIPPED MUTANT. A skipped
mutant is a FAILURE -- the run exits non-zero -- so a spec that has
drifted can never be mistaken for a clean run. That rule IS kept on
this path.
* A vitest run in which EVERY TEST IS SKIPPED is a different thing, and
it used to be reported as 'mutant SURVIVED': vitest exits 0, the
harness found the 'Tests N skipped' summary and read it as a pass.
That was a false green. The harness now reports an all-skipped run as
BROKEN and aborts (rc=3), so the run exits 2. The rule lives in
tools/mutation_harness.py:summary_ran_no_test() and is pinned by
tests/test_mutation_harness_skip.py.
What is covered here and NOT in oracle_availability_truth.json:
* frontend/src/lib/oracleCapability.ts -- the WEB client's decision
module. The web client is a separate application from the PWA and
cannot import its product code, so it has its own module; the test
that PROVES the two agree runs both against the same inputs.
* pwa/lib/oracleCapability.ts -- the PWA's own decision module.
* pwa/components/LaunchStrategyModal.tsx -- the launch that used to
substitute DYNAMIC_NATR for a saved DYNAMIC_ORACLE strategy.
ALSO COVERED HERE, AND ALSO IN oracle_availability_truth.json (the two
specs run different runners, so the same defect is caught twice):
* pwa/screens/StrategiesScreen.tsx -- the launch PAYLOAD. The truth
spec asserts it at SOURCE level, because the PWA screen cannot be
imported by the pytest path at all. Here it is asserted as
BEHAVIOUR: src/__tests__/pwaStrategiesPayload.test.tsx renders the
screen and reads the payload the SERVER RECEIVES.
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/oracle_availability_web.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.
RUN IT WITH PYTHONUTF8=1 ON WINDOWS.
The harness's `run_command` calls subprocess.run(..., text=True) with no
encoding, so it decodes the child's output with the LOCALE encoding --
cp1252 on a default Windows box. vitest writes UTF-8 (its box-drawing and
check glyphs) and cp1252 cannot decode byte 0x9d, so the reader thread
raised UnicodeDecodeError, no output was captured, the harness found no
test summary and ABORTED with rc=3. MEASURED: with PYTHONUTF8=1 the same
command decodes the output intact and the 'Test Files' summary is read.
That is why the harness file is NOT patched for this: the environment
setting fixes it, so the harness stays byte-identical to the commit it
was taken from.
$env:PYTHONUTF8='1'
python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/oracle_availability_web.json

mutations.label: R: the WEB client invents a 95% threshold when the server declares none
mutations.replace: return 95; // MUTANT: the client invents a threshold

mutations.label: S: the WEB client says the oracle is usable whenever the server answered at all
mutations.replace: return capability != null; // MUTANT: any answer means available

mutations.label: T: the WEB client invents oracle regime 1
U: the PWA sends 0 again, and the server reads 0 as NO threshold
mutations.replace: return 0; // MUTANT: the client sends 0 and the server reads it as 'no threshold'

mutations.label: V: the PWA switches the symbol-selection mode behind the customer's back
mutations.replace: if (false) { // MUTANT: the mode is substituted instead

mutations.label: W: the client no longer refuses a saved oracle strategy when the oracle is gone
X: the PWA's launch PAYLOAD invents a 95% confidence again
Y: the PWA's launch PAYLOAD invents oracle regime 1 again
